questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses inversion in a condition to express strong emphasis on the subject’s action?
options: It was not until she finished her work that she realised the importance of the project.
Only when she had finished her work did she realise how critical the project was.
She realised the project was critical only after she had finished her work.
Having finished her work, she realised it was not important at all.
questions.answer: Only when she had finished her work did she realise how critical the project was.

questions.question: Which cleft sentence correctly rephrases the following sentence while maintaining the original meaning: 'The reason we left early was because of the traffic.'?
options: It was the traffic that made us leave early because we had to.
The reason we left early was because of the traffic; it was the traffic that caused us to leave.
Because of the traffic, it was the reason we left early; we had no choice.
The reason we left early was because of the traffic, and the traffic was the cause.
questions.answer: The reason we left early was because of the traffic; it was the traffic that caused us to leave.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a hypothetical scenario where a wish or unreal condition is implied?
options: If she were to win the competition, she would be very happy.
She would be very happy if she wins the competition.
If she wins the competition, she will be very happy.
She wishes she would win the competition, but she doesn’t believe it will happen.
questions.answer: If she were to win the competition, she would be very happy.

questions.question: Which sentence demonstrates correct use of ellipsis and formal register to avoid redundancy while maintaining clarity in a professional context?
options: She said she would be here by 5 PM, but she didn’t show up. Instead, she left a message.
Having failed to arrive by the deadline, she sent an apology email.
She apologised for not meeting the deadline, but she didn’t provide an explanation.
It was disappointing that she didn’t follow through on her promise, but she didn’t give a reason.
questions.answer: Having failed to arrive by the deadline, she sent an apology email.

questions.question: Which sentence correctly employs a complex conditional structure to express a situation where an action would be appropriate under certain hypothetical circumstances?
options: If you had studied harder, you would have passed the exam.
She would have passed the exam if she had studied harder, but she didn’t.
If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam, but she didn’t bother.
Had she studied harder, she would have passed the exam, but she didn’t try.
questions.answer: Had she studied harder, she would have passed the exam, but she didn’t try.
